Bayesian optimization of a simulation study

Source: R/tune.R
tune_bayes.Rd

Like tune::tune_bayes(). Starts from initial space-filling designs, then proposes one design per iteration by expected improvement under a Gaussian process fitted to design means (with Monte Carlo standard errors as noise). With constraints, improvement is weighted by the modeled probability that each constrained metric meets its bound, so "the cheapest design with at least 80% power" is answered directly: metrics = sim_metric_set(cost, power), constraints = list(power = 0.8).

Usage

tune_bayes(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'sim_spec'
tune_bayes(
  object,
  resamples = NULL,
  ...,
  metrics = NULL,
  param_info = NULL,
  initial = 6,
  iter = 10,
  metric = NULL,
  constraints = NULL,
  no_improve = Inf,
  candidates = 2000,
  control = control_sim(),
  seed = 1
)

Arguments

object

A simulation spec with tune() arguments.

...

Not used.

resamples

Replicates from sim_replicates(), or a number of replicates.

metrics

A sim_metric_set(); defaults to the spec's own.

param_info

A dials parameters object with changed ranges, from extract_parameter_set_dials(spec) |> update(...).

initial

Number of starting designs, or a data frame of them.

iter

Number of proposals after the initial designs.

metric

The metric to race on; defaults to the first in the set.

constraints

Named list of bounds on other metrics' means, e.g. list(power = 0.8). A bare number is a floor for metrics to maximize and a ceiling for metrics to minimize; list(cost = c("<=", 5000)) is explicit.

no_improve

Stop after this many iterations without a new best design.

candidates

Size of the random candidate pool scored at each iteration.

control

A control_sim() object.

seed

Seed for generating the space-filling grid.

Value

A sim_results object; x$trace lists each proposal.
